sourceEvidence.text: English blouse was borrowed from French blouse, a loose protective smock worn by workers or peasants. The garment name later became fashionable for women and children. The French word’s earlier origin is unknown; suggestions involving other languages or an Egyptian place name remain proposals. The attested garment meaning is usable, but neither a confident remote chain nor an English blou-/se split is justified.
